boundary_decision.rationale: Both independent providers model version/change history as reusable context attached to a host entity or specification series. The host, lifecycle state machine, provenance graph, identifier scheme, representation format and execution platform remain separate models connected by typed references.

decisions.rationale: Grok independently covers the same revision identity, predecessor/version set, compatibility/lifecycle and change-history/migration concerns. Claude separates lineage, change substance, temporal lifecycle, authority/integrity and access/retention more precisely without losing Grok coverage.

decisions.concept: Version / Change History is a host-bound mixin
decisions.rationale: A version record identifies and relates snapshots or revisions of a host series without redefining the host domain object.

decisions.concept: Mutable series/permalink and immutable revision are the same identity
decisions.rationale: The version-independent series, a current pointer and each frozen revision have different identity, dereference, citation and integrity semantics.

decisions.concept: Every related edition, translation, rendition or derivation is a version
decisions.rationale: Revision, derivation, translation, format variant, alternate and specialization use typed relations and can have different entity identity.

decisions.concept: One previous-version link is a complete history
decisions.rationale: Merge, branch, backport, cherry-pick and composed releases require a predecessor set and graph integrity; linear projection must report loss.
A designation scheme states an intended promise. Actual backward/forward/full compatibility must name producer/consumer scope, surface, evidence, exceptions and migration obligations.

decisions.concept: Patch or diff format is the logical model
decisions.rationale: JSON Patch, Git diffs, schema migrations and database updates are version-pinned projections of a logical source-target change set with preconditions, atomicity, loss and verification.

decisions.concept: Version identifier derived from publication timestamp
decisions.rationale: Use a master-system or governed scheme identifier; timestamps are separate RFC 3339 facts with seconds and explicit timezone.

decisions.concept: Released content may change in place
decisions.rationale: A frozen revision has immutable identity and fixity evidence. Correction creates a new revision or explicit amendment and preserves tamper-evident history.

decisions.concept: Delete, withdraw, deprecate, supersede and redact are equivalent
decisions.rationale: They differ in current-pointer behavior, consumer warning, availability, integrity, retention, privacy and evidence obligations.

deferred_research: Formal semantic-diff calculi and compatibility proofs for ontologies, database schemas, event schemas and executable APIs.
Distributed version graphs, offline replicas, CRDT history, signed transparency logs and consensus rules.
Composite release/version identity across many independently versioned child models and dependency lock sets.
Jurisdiction-specific retention, erasure, legal hold and evidentiary requirements for historical versions.
Binary delta, reproducible build and software supply-chain profiles beyond logical alignment.
publication_holds: Verify live editions and claim-level support for all accepted W3C, DCMI, DCAT, PROV, PAV, DataCite, IETF, SemVer and migration sources.
Validate round-trip identity, DAG history, compatibility and migration semantics against at least five host profiles: Vercy specifications, APIs, database schemas, documents and software releases.
